title: malvaviscus arboreus var. longifolius
intro: Malvaviscus arboreus var. longifolius, commonly known as the Mexican hibiscus or musk mallow, is a plant species native to the tropical regions of Central and South America. It has been used in traditional medicine for its various health benefits, including its ability to treat fever, wounds, and skin conditions, such as eczema and acne. The therapeutic actions of Malvaviscus arboreus var. longifolius include its anti-inflammatory, antimicrobial, and antioxidant properties, which help to soothe and calm the skin. The plant's bioactive constituents include flavonoids, alkaloids, and glycosides, which are responsible for its medicinal properties.
